_note: Hand-written cases for core/reading/decide.decide_printing (rule A2): the evidence in, the answer a person working the rule out by hand expects. NOT produced by running the code. Similarities are binary fractions (0.875, 0.859375 = 0.875 - 1/64, 0.84375 = 0.875 - 1/32, 0.8125 = 0.875 - 1/16) so that every gap and lead is exact. Default thresholds: agree_below 0.02, image_lead 0.05. A candidate names the strip's printing when its plain number AND its lower-cased set equal the strip's; the first such candidate (nearest first) is the only one looked at. Any program that decides the same way must pass these files too.

cases.name: strip names the best match
cases.why: the strip's printing is the nearest: it is confirmed by the picture

cases.name: strip names a reprint with the same art, second nearest
cases.why: B looks as much like the picture as A (a gap of 1/64, under 0.02): the strip decides between the two reprints

cases.name: strip names a printing that looks different (a Secret Lair card)
cases.why: the printed line names another printing, with other art: the strip is not believed, the picture decides (lead 0.5)

cases.name: strip names a printing that is not among the candidates
cases.why: nothing to confirm it with: the picture alone

cases.name: no strip, a clear lead
cases.why: the best match leads the second by 1/16 = 0.0625, at least 0.05

cases.name: no strip, no lead (two reprints with one art)
cases.why: the picture cannot tell A from B and there is nothing else: review

cases.name: strip names the second nearest but it is not close enough, and the lead is small
cases.why: B names the strip but is 1/32 = 0.03125 below A (not under 0.02): not believed; the lead is 0.03125 (under 0.05): review

cases.name: leading zeros and the case of the set
cases.why: the database writes '0172' and 'HOB', the strip reads '172' and 'hob': the same printing

cases.name: only a number was read
cases.why: a printing is named by its number AND its set: with one of them the strip names nothing; the picture alone

cases.name: only a set was read
cases.why: as above

cases.name: no candidates (no image index)
cases.why: nothing to decide with

cases.name: one candidate, and the strip names it
cases.why: the strip's printing is the picture's only candidate: strong (there is no second one, so no lead)

cases.name: one candidate, no strip
cases.why: no lead can be measured with one candidate: review

cases.name: two candidates name the strip's printing equally
cases.why: the nearest comes first and is the one looked at: A

cases.name: a candidate without a set or a number never names anything
cases.why: A has no set and no number; B names the strip but is far below A: not believed; the picture decides

cases.name: a card found upside down is decided like any other
cases.why: the flag only says how the strip was read; the decision is the same as the first case

cases.name: boundary: a gap equal to agree_below is not agreement
cases.why: thresholds 0.25 / 0.5, B is exactly 0.25 below A: the test is 'less than', so it is not believed; the lead 0.25 is under 0.5: review

cases.name: boundary: a gap just under agree_below is agreement
cases.why: thresholds 0.25 / 0.5, B is 0.1875 below A (under 0.25): strong

cases.name: boundary: a lead equal to image_lead is enough
cases.why: thresholds 0.25 / 0.5, the lead is exactly 0.5: 'at least', so the picture is believed

cases.name: negative similarities
cases.why: similarity runs from -1 to 1; only differences matter: the lead is 0.25

cases.name: the strip's set is expected in lower case
cases.why: the parse of the strip writes the set lower case (card_ocr.parse_strip); an upper-case 'TST' names nothing: the picture decides
